_comment: STRIP THIS KEY BEFORE USE. The AWS CLI rejects unknown members in
--cli-input-json, so _comment makes create-service fail with 'Unknown
parameter in input'. The runbook does it in one line and it is the only
preprocessing needed:
jq 'del(._comment) | .SourceConfiguration.AuthenticationConfiguration.AccessRoleArn = $arn' \
--arg arn "$ACCESS_ROLE_ARN" apprunner-service.json > /tmp/apprunner-input.json
aws apprunner create-service --cli-input-json file:///tmp/apprunner-input.json
Mirrors the labs service (labs.demohouse.cloud), which is a real running
App Runner service in this account on an ECR image at 1024/2048.
Replace <ACCESS_ROLE_ARN> with the role App Runner assumes to pull from ECR;
docs/lf-control-loops-deploy.md step 3 creates it. Everything else is final.
Health check is GET /api/healthz, not /. Confirmed against app/main.py, not
assumed: `@app.get("/api/healthz")` is declared at main.py:277, returns
{"ok": true}, and is declared BEFORE the `app.mount("/", StaticFiles(...))` at
main.py:356, which matters because the catch-all static mount would otherwise
shadow it and answer 404. / serves the SPA through that mount, and a health
check on a loop endpoint would call OpenAI or Langfuse -- which would take this
service down every time a third party has a bad day, and, since there are no
server-side keys, would fail permanently. healthz answers 200 with no
credentials and touches nothing external.
AutoScalingConfigurationArn caps the bill. READ THIS BEFORE REMOVING IT.
App Runner's CreateService API takes only an ARN here; there is no inline
MinSize/MaxSize/MaxConcurrency to put in this file. Omitting the field is not
neutral: the API then attaches the default configuration, which is MaxSize 25.
This app is public and unauthenticated, has no rate limit and no concurrency
cap of its own, and a review demonstrated one unauthenticated caller saturating
an instance in about two minutes. Bring-your-own-key means such a caller cannot
spend OUR OpenAI or Langfuse quota -- that half of the argument holds and was
verified -- but it does nothing about OUR App Runner compute and egress bill,
which is what a scale-to-25 default turns a flood into. So the ceiling is
deliberately 2, not 25. See docs/lf-control-loops-deploy.md step 3b for the
create-auto-scaling-configuration call that must run BEFORE create-service,
and for the per-number confidence notes. create-service fails loudly if the
configuration does not exist yet, which is the failure mode we want: a missing
ceiling should stop the deploy, not silently become 25.
The ARN deliberately carries no trailing revision number, so the service tracks
the latest revision of that configuration name. Appending /1 would pin it and
make a later ceiling change a service update instead of a config revision.
Note the absence of a RuntimeEnvironmentVariables or RuntimeEnvironmentSecrets
block. That is not an omission to fill in later: this app holds no server-side
credential at all. OpenAI and Langfuse keys arrive per request in X-OpenAI-Key /
X-Langfuse-* headers from the visitor's own browser session. So there is no
Secrets Manager entry to provision, no instance role needing secretsmanager or
ssm permissions, no rotation runbook, and no blast radius if the image leaks.
The service needs an ACCESS role to pull the image and no INSTANCE role at all.
AutoDeploymentsEnabled is false to match labs: an ECR push must not ship
itself. The CI workflow builds and pushes; a human runs start-deployment.
Architecture is X86_64. App Runner does not run arm64 images, so do not copy
the --platform linux/arm64 build from .github/workflows/workshop.yml, which
targets a Graviton EC2 host instead.
